extracted.subtask_description: Reviewer guidelines for evaluating AISTATS 2026 paper submissions: responsibilities, required declarations, review-form evaluation dimensions (soundness, significance, novelty, etc.), and procedural expectations for rebuttal, discussion, and ethics. Intended to guide reviewers in producing high-quality, timely, and ethical reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of a Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Report problematic papers to the Area Chair (e.g., unacceptable formatting issues, dual submissions, plagiarism, etc.); submit high-quality reviews; during the rebuttal period, discuss with the other reviewers and the AC to help arrive at a good decision; recommend papers for oral talks, awards, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you encounter issues (plagiarism, dual submission, formatting), report them to the AC rather than handling them alone; participate in rebuttal and reviewer-AC discussions; provide recommendations for talks/awards as part of your review responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for writing reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Be thoughtful. Be fair. Be useful. Be specific. Be flexible. Be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember some authors may be submitting for the first time; avoid letting personal feelings affect your review; give constructive feedback useful to authors, reviewers, and ACs; avoid vague comments; update your review when new information is presented; meet deadlines and respond promptly during discussions. If pressured to bias your review, notify Program Chairs via the official contact form; report unethical or suspicious behavior to your Area Chair immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep the paper and supplementary materials (including code submissions and LaTeX source), as well as the reviews, confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delete any submitted code at the end of the review cycle to comply with confidentiality requirements. Do not share the manuscript with other people or LLM services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct / Declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must confirm that the review is written by them (and not, e.g., an LLM) and that they do not have any known conflicts with the authors (e.g., participating in a collusion circle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By accepting, reviewers agree to abide by the AISTATS Code of Conduct and the Reviewer Guidelines; visible confirmations may be required on the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the theoretical arguments and/or empirical methods sound? Consider whether the assumptions, proofs, and derivations are correct, and whether the experimental design, evaluation, and analysis are rigorous and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: Correct / minor errors (e.g., typo or errors that do not affect the main results); Major errors (e.g., an incorrect theorem or derivation); Not applicable. Provide a justification describing details of any errors or why the judgment was made. If not applicable, put 'N/A'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of the contributions (theoretical and/or empirical, if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: Significant contributions (e.g., strong theoretical insights or well-supported empirical improvements with appropriate baselines/statistics); Somewhat significant (e.g., theoretical contribution of limited novelty or empirical gains missing baselines/statistical rigor); Not significant (e.g., theoretical results are incremental, or empirical results are similar to baselines/missing key comparisons); Not applicable. Provide justification; if 'somewhat significant' or 'not significant', specify concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty of the theoretical results and/or empirical methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: Ground-breaking; New results; Incremental compared to existing results; Known results, or a trivial extension of known results. Provide justification. If choosing 'incremental' or 'known results' please specify previous publication(s) that support your choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-conventional Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission contain non-conventional research contributions? Examples: novel ideas with not widely accepted assumptions, new problems and/or tasks, 'bridging fields' contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field to report merits that do not fit under other review form fields; include a short justification explaining why the contribution is non-conventional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written? Consider whether it has (1) clearly stated its contributions, notation and results, (2) supported the claims made in the title, abstract, introduction with results, (3) explained the meaning of its theoretical assumptions, and/or (4) motivated the proposed methodology well with e.g., examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether exposition enables understanding of contributions and technical content; point to unclear sections and suggest improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation To Prior Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clearly discussed how this work differs from or relates to prior work in the literature? Any related work missing (if yes, provide details below)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: All related works are clearly discussed; All related works are cited but the discussion is less clear; Some minor related works are missing or described incorrectly; Some important related works are missing or described incorrectly. If works are missing or misdescribed, provide details and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and Contributions (review form field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary so authors, ACs, and other reviewers understand your interpretation of the submission and basis for your judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Keywords and Expertise Keywords (review form fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper Keywords: Provide 3 keywords about the paper’s topic. Expertise Keywords: Provide 3 keywords about your own research expertise related to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comma-separated keywords to help matching and indicate reviewer expertise. Be specific and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments (for authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add your additional comments, feedback, and suggestions for improvement, as well as any further questions for the authors. What would you do differently if you were given the chance to improve the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this optional field to give constructive, actionable feedback to authors. Focus on points that can help improve clarity, experiments, or positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Comments (to Area Chair)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments for the Area Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this optional field to raise private concerns to the AC (e.g., suspected ethical issues, conflicts, or sensitive matters not suitable for author-facing comments). Visible only to PCs/SACs/ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there enough details to reproduce the main experimental results of this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: Sufficient amount of details available for reproducing the main results; Some amount of details available; Insufficient amount of details available; Not applicable (the paper does not have experiments). Provide specifics on missing details (hyperparameters, seeds, dataset processing, code availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Rating (7-point scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall rating of the paper from 7 (Strong Accept) to 1 (Strong Reject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7: Strong Accept — Technically excellent paper with clear novelty and broad potential impact beyond a single sub-area; 6: Accept — Technically solid paper, with high impact on at least one sub-area; 5: Borderline Accept — reasons to accept outweigh reasons to reject; 4: Weak Accept / Weak Reject — paper has some merits but also notable weaknesses; 3: Borderline Reject — reasons to reject outweigh reasons to accept; 2: Reject — technical flaws, weak evaluation, inadequate reproducibility and incompletely addressed ethical considerations; 1: Strong Reject — well-known results or unaddressed ethical considerations. Use descriptions to justify your numeric rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence level of the reviewer in their evaluation (5 to 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5: Absolutely certain (use sparingly); 4: Confident, but not absolutely certain; 3: Fairly confident; 2: Somewhat confident; 1: Educated guess (not in your area). Use this to indicate how carefully proofs/experiments/related work were checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this submission raise potential ethical concerns? These include methods, applications, or data that create or reinforce unfair biases and/or that have a primary purpose of harm or injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of: No concern; Minor concerns; Major concerns. Provide justification for your judgement. (Field visible only to PCs/SACs/ACs.) If you believe someone is engaging in unethical conduct, notify AISTATS via the official contact form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Generative AI in Reviewing (prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strictly prohibited to use Generative AI tools, such as large language models (LLMs), for reviewing AISTATS submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cannot use Generative AI tools to write their reviews, and reviewers cannot input any content from any submission or review into a Generative AI tool. Report suspected violations to the official contact form; violations may be investigated and sanctioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Rebuttal and Discussion Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be given the opportunity to respond to reviews. Reviewers are expected to read and (if appropriate) respond to each author’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an open mind during the discussion period; do not ignore any author response even if you plan to reject. If an author’s response did not change your assessment, explicitly convey that you carefully considered their comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Supplementary Material, External Links, and Submitted Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material may be appended; conflicts between appended and separately uploaded material can be resolved at the reviewer’s discretion. Exercise caution when accessing external links. Reviewing submitted code is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose to access submitted code, ensure anonymity and be aware of possible security risks. Resolve inconsistencies between appended and separately uploaded material sensibly; do not assume external links are safe or anonymized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor formatting issues — do not desk-reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor formatting issues should not be a reason to desk-reject a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag minor formatting problems to the Area Chair instead of desk-rejecting; focus review judgments on technical/content merits rather than small format errors.
